newsitem.title: USA: Pomeroy Q1 revs up 59 pct to $100.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Pomeroy Q1 revs up 59 pct to $100.7 mln.

text.p: Pomeroy Computer Resources Inc said Monday revenues for the first quarter ended April 5, 1997 were about $100.7 million, an increase of 59.3 percent from the comparable first quarter in 1996.
The stock was up $1 to 19-7/8 in mid-afternoon trading.
Pomeroy also said it signed a deal with International Business Machines Corp to become an authorized assembler of IBM computer products for corporate customers.
The company said it will stock a wide variety of IBM components instead of completed systems, allowing it to customize customer orders without hurting order lead times.
The deal also allows Pomeroy to assemble and sell IBM systems to smaller computer resellers.
For the year ended Jan. 5, 1997, the company reported revenues of $336.4 million. Revenues for the fourth quarter ended January 5, 1997 were $102.3 million.
Pomeroy said it expects to release earnings in late April.
Pomeroy Computer provides computer integration services from facilities in Kentucky, Ohio, Indiana, Iowa, Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina, Alabama and Florida.
